views.name: player_min_potential
views.body_sql:
SELECT *
FROM Player_Attributes
WHERE potential = (SELECT MIN(potential) FROM Player_Attributes)
views.description: Relation of players whose potential equals the minimum potential across all players (returns player attributes for those with global min potential).

provenance.question: What is the preferred foot when attacking of the player with the lowest potential?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the preferred_foot value for the player(s) whose potential is equal to the minimum potential across all players.
Required outputs: preferred_foot
Filters: potential = MIN(potential) across all rows

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows for the declared grain 'id' (each id appears at most once in the view).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM player_min_potential GROUP BY id HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Every row in the view has potential equal to the global minimum potential in the base table Player_Attributes.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_min_potential v WHERE v.potential <> (SELECT MIN(potential) FROM Player_Attributes) OR v.potential IS NULL

tests.purpose: The view did not introduce rows whose id does not exist in the base table Player_Attributes (every id in view must exist in base).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_min_potential v WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Player_Attributes p WHERE p.id = v.id)

views.name: player_max_crossing
views.body_sql: SELECT player_api_id AS player_id, MAX(crossing) AS crossing FROM Player_Attributes GROUP BY player_api_id
views.description: Per-player maximum crossing attribute value across all entries in Player_Attributes, useful for ranking players by their best observed crossing ability.

provenance.question: Who are the top 5 players who perform better in crossing actions? Indicate their player id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the top 5 players (by player id) who have the highest value of crossing, where 'perform better in crossing actions' is defined as the maximum crossing value.
Required outputs: player id; crossing (the crossing value used to rank players)
Filters: consider all players in the dataset (no other row filters)
Sort/limit: order by crossing descending, limit 5

tests.purpose: No duplicate player_id rows in the view (view grain is player_id)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT player_id FROM player_max_crossing GROUP BY player_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1)

tests.purpose: Each view row's crossing equals the MAX(crossing) computed from Player_Attributes for that player_id
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_max_crossing v LEFT JOIN (SELECT player_api_id AS player_id, MAX(crossing) AS expected_crossing FROM Player_Attributes GROUP BY player_api_id) b ON v.player_id = b.player_id WHERE (b.expected_crossing IS NULL AND v.crossing IS NOT NULL) OR (b.expected_crossing IS NOT NULL AND v.crossing IS NULL) OR (b.expected_crossing IS NOT NULL AND v.crossing <> b.expected_crossing)

tests.purpose: Every player_id in the view exists in Player_Attributes (no dangling keys)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_max_crossing v WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Player_Attributes p WHERE p.player_api_id = v.player_id)

views.name: league_total_goals_per_season
views.body_sql: SELECT L.id AS league_id, L.name AS league_name, M.season AS season, SUM(COALESCE(M.home_team_goal,0) + COALESCE(M.away_team_goal,0)) AS total_goals FROM Match M JOIN League L ON M.league_id = L.id GROUP BY L.id, L.name, M.season
views.description: Per-league total goals in a season computed as the sum of home and away goals across all matches belonging to the league (one row per league per season).

provenance.question: Which league had the most goals in the 2016 season?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find which league (i.e., the league identifier/name) had the highest total number of goals scored in all matches during the 2015/2016 season, where total goals for a league is computed as the sum across its matches of (home_team_goal + away_team_goal).
Required outputs: league (identifier or name as available in the schema); total_goals (the sum of home_team_goal + away_team_goal across all matches in that league for the specified season)
Filters: season = '2015/2016'; only include matches that belong to a league (as per schema relationship between matches and leagues)
Sort/limit: order by total_goals DESC limit 1

tests.purpose: View has one row per league_id, league_name, season (no duplicate keys).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT league_id, league_name, season, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM league_total_goals_per_season GROUP BY league_id, league_name, season HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: total_goals equals the sum of home + away goals aggregated from Match for that league and season.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM league_total_goals_per_season v LEFT JOIN (SELECT M.league_id AS league_id, M.season AS season, SUM(COALESCE(M.home_team_goal,0) + COALESCE(M.away_team_goal,0)) AS expected_total FROM Match M GROUP BY M.league_id, M.season) s ON v.league_id = s.league_id AND v.season = s.season WHERE (s.expected_total IS NULL AND v.total_goals IS NOT NULL) OR (s.expected_total IS NOT NULL AND (v.total_goals IS NULL OR v.total_goals != s.expected_total))

tests.purpose: Keys league_id, league_name, season are not NULL in the view.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM league_total_goals_per_season WHERE league_id IS NULL OR league_name IS NULL OR season IS NULL

views.name: home_team_season_home_loss_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT m.season, m.home_team_api_id AS home_team_api_id, t.team_long_name AS home_team_long_name, COUNT(m.id) AS home_losses FROM "Match" m JOIN "Team" t ON m.home_team_api_id = t.team_api_id WHERE (m.home_team_goal - m.away_team_goal) < 0 GROUP BY m.season, m.home_team_api_id, t.team_long_name
views.description: Counts of home losses per home team for each season (number of matches where home_team_goal - away_team_goal < 0), keeping team identifiers for joins

provenance.question: Which home team had lost the fewest matches in the 2016 season?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the home team (team name) that had the fewest number of losses in home matches during the 2015/2016 season, where a home loss is defined as home_team_goal - away_team_goal < 0.
Required outputs: home_team (the name/identifier of the home team); home_losses (the count of matches in that season where home_team_goal - away_team_goal < 0 for that home_team)
Filters: season = '2015/2016'; consider only matches where home_team_goal - away_team_goal < 0 for counting a home loss
Sort/limit: order by home_losses asc limit 1

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the view grain (season, home_team_api_id, home_team_long_name).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM home_team_season_home_loss_counts v WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM home_team_season_home_loss_counts v2 WHERE v2.season = v.season AND v2.home_team_api_id = v.home_team_api_id AND v2.home_team_long_name = v.home_team_long_name) > 1

tests.purpose: home_losses equals the number of Match rows for that season/team where home_team_goal - away_team_goal < 0 (measure reconciles with base table).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM home_team_season_home_loss_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT m.season, m.home_team_api_id, t.team_long_name AS home_team_long_name, COUNT(m.id) AS expected_home_losses FROM "Match" m JOIN "Team" t ON m.home_team_api_id = t.team_api_id WHERE (m.home_team_goal - m.away_team_goal) < 0 GROUP BY m.season, m.home_team_api_id, t.team_long_name) b ON v.season = b.season AND v.home_team_api_id = b.home_team_api_id AND v.home_team_long_name = b.home_team_long_name WHERE (b.expected_home_losses IS NULL AND v.home_losses IS NOT NULL) OR (b.expected_home_losses IS NOT NULL AND v.home_losses != b.expected_home_losses)

tests.purpose: Keys (season, home_team_api_id, home_team_long_name) are not NULL.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM home_team_season_home_loss_counts v WHERE v.season IS NULL OR v.home_team_api_id IS NULL OR v.home_team_long_name IS NULL

views.name: matches_per_league
views.body_sql: SELECT m.league_id AS league_id, COUNT(*) AS match_count FROM Match m GROUP BY m.league_id
views.description: Total number of Match rows grouped by league (one row per league with league_id and match count), useful for ranking or filtering leagues by match volume.

provenance.question: Give the name of the league with the highest matches of all time and how many matches were played in the said league.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the league (League.name) that has the largest total number of matches (count of Match rows grouped by league_id) and return that league's name and the corresponding match count.
Required outputs: league_name: the League.name value for the league with the maximum total matches; match_count: an integer equal to the total number of Match rows that have that league's id
Filters: Consider all Match rows (no additional WHERE conditions); group matches by Match.league_id; Count matches per league using COUNT(Match.*) or COUNT(*) for each league_id; Select the league_id whose count equals the maximum count across all leagues: COUNT(Match) = MAX(COUNT(Match) over each league); Join to League on League.id = Match.league_id to obtain League.name
Sort/limit: order results by match_count DESC and limit to 1 (return the single league with the highest match_count)

tests.purpose: View has one row per league_id (no duplicate league_id values)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT league_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM matches_per_league GROUP BY league_id HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: match_count equals actual number of Match rows per league_id
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM matches_per_league v LEFT JOIN (SELECT league_id, COUNT(*) AS expected_count FROM "Match" GROUP BY league_id) b ON v.league_id = b.league_id WHERE b.expected_count IS NULL OR v.match_count <> b.expected_count

tests.purpose: league_id (the key) is never NULL in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM matches_per_league WHERE league_id IS NULL

views.name: league_total_goals
views.body_sql:
SELECT L.id AS league_id, L.name AS league_name, SUM(M.home_team_goal + M.away_team_goal) AS total_goals
FROM Match M
JOIN League L ON M.league_id = L.id
WHERE M.home_team_goal IS NOT NULL
  AND M.away_team_goal IS NOT NULL
  AND L.id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY L.id, L.name
views.description: Per-league total goals aggregated across all matches by summing home and away goals for matches with non-null goal values and valid league ids.

provenance.question: List the top 5 leagues in ascending order of the number of goals made in all seasons combined.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Compute each league's total number of goals across all seasons by summing home_team_goal and away_team_goal for every match, then return the top 5 leagues with the smallest total goals (ascending order).
Required outputs: league (identifier/name as provided in the data); total_goals (integer) — the sum over all seasons of home_team_goal + away_team_goal for matches in that league
Filters: Include all matches from all seasons (no season filtering).; Aggregate by league.; Exclude leagues with null or missing league identifier or where goal values are null in a way that prevents accurate summation (only include matches with non-null numeric home_team_goal and away_team_goal).
Sort/limit: Order by total_goals ASC (ascending). Limit to 5 rows.

tests.purpose: No NULL keys: league_id or league_name should never be NULL in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM league_total_goals WHERE league_id IS NULL OR league_name IS NULL

tests.purpose: Aggregation correctness: total_goals equals sum of home_team_goal+away_team_goal from Match for matches with non-null goals and matching league
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM league_total_goals LTG LEFT JOIN (SELECT M.league_id AS league_id, SUM(M.home_team_goal + M.away_team_goal) AS expected_total FROM Match M JOIN League L ON M.league_id = L.id WHERE M.home_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND M.away_team_goal IS NOT NULL AND L.id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY M.league_id) AS S ON LTG.league_id = S.league_id WHERE (S.expected_total IS NULL AND (LTG.total_goals IS NOT NULL AND LTG.total_goals<>0)) OR (S.expected_total IS NOT NULL AND (LTG.total_goals IS NULL OR LTG.total_goals<>S.expected_total))

tests.purpose: No duplicate grains: there should be at most one row per (league_id, league_name)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT league_id, league_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM league_total_goals GROUP BY league_id, league_name HAVING cnt>1)

views.name: player_average_heading_accuracy
views.body_sql:
SELECT p.player_fifa_api_id, p.player_name, p.height, SUM(pa.heading_accuracy) * 1.0 / COUNT(pa.player_fifa_api_id) AS average_heading_accuracy
FROM Player p
JOIN Player_Attributes pa
  ON p.player_fifa_api_id = pa.player_fifa_api_id
WHERE pa.heading_accuracy IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY p.player_fifa_api_id, p.player_name, p.height
views.description: Per-player average heading accuracy computed from Player_Attributes joined to Player, for players with any heading_accuracy records and including player identifiers and height for filtering/joins.
counter_examples: What's the heading accuracy of Ariel Borysiuk?

provenance.question: List the top 10 players' names whose heights are above 180 in descending order of average heading accuracy.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Return the top 10 players whose heights are greater than 180, ranked by their average heading accuracy in descending order; average heading accuracy is defined as SUM(heading_accuracy) divided by COUNT(player_fifa_api_id).
Required outputs: player_name; average_heading_accuracy (numeric computed as DIVIDE(SUM(heading_accuracy), COUNT(player_fifa_api_id)))
Filters: height > 180; Include only players for whom heading_accuracy values exist (i.e., COUNT(player_fifa_api_id) > 0)
Sort/limit: ORDER BY average_heading_accuracy DESC LIMIT 10

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (player_fifa_api_id, player_name, height).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT player_fifa_api_id, player_name, height, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM player_average_heading_accuracy GROUP BY player_fifa_api_id, player_name, height HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: average_heading_accuracy matches recomputed average from Player_Attributes for each player (only consider rows where base has non-NULL heading_accuracy).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_average_heading_accuracy v LEFT JOIN (SELECT pa.player_fifa_api_id, AVG(pa.heading_accuracy * 1.0) AS recomputed_avg FROM Player_Attributes pa WHERE pa.heading_accuracy IS NOT NULL GROUP BY pa.player_fifa_api_id) r ON v.player_fifa_api_id = r.player_fifa_api_id WHERE (r.recomputed_avg IS NULL AND v.average_heading_accuracy IS NOT NULL) OR (r.recomputed_avg IS NOT NULL AND ABS(v.average_heading_accuracy - r.recomputed_avg) > 1e-6)

tests.purpose: Every view row corresponds to an existing Player and the join did not introduce NULL keys: player_fifa_api_id, player_name, height must be non-NULL and player must exist in Player.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_average_heading_accuracy v LEFT JOIN Player p ON v.player_fifa_api_id = p.player_fifa_api_id WHERE v.player_fifa_api_id IS NULL OR v.player_name IS NULL OR v.height IS NULL OR p.player_fifa_api_id IS NULL

negative_subgoals:
Task: Compute Ariel Borysiuk's heading accuracy — the percentage (or fraction) of his headed attempts that were successful (i.e., headed shots/goals completed) as recorded in the dataset.
Required outputs: player_name: the player name (Ariel Borysiuk); heading_accuracy: a numeric value representing heading accuracy (percentage or fraction) as stored in the data, with units if applicable
Filters: player_name = 'Ariel Borysiuk'; only consider records/statistics that measure heading accuracy or fields that represent headed attempts and successful headers (use the table/columns that represent heading accuracy or the numerator/denominator for headers)

views.name: league_season_home_away_goal_averages
views.body_sql:
SELECT M.league_id, L.name AS league_name, M.season, AVG(M.home_team_goal) AS avg_home_goals, AVG(M.away_team_goal) AS avg_away_goals
FROM "Match" M
JOIN League L ON M.league_id = L.id
GROUP BY M.league_id, L.name, M.season
views.description: Average home and away goals per league per season (one row per league-season) to compare scoring rates by venue.

provenance.question: List the name of leagues in which the average goals by the home team is higher than the away team in the 2009/2010 season.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find all League.name values for leagues where, considering matches in the 2009/2010 season, the average of home_team_goal is greater than the average of away_team_goal.
Required outputs: League.name
Filters: season = '2009/2010'; AVG(home_team_goal) > AVG(away_team_goal) computed over matches in the same league and season

tests.purpose: No duplicate league-season rows (view grain is one row per league_id, league_name, season).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM league_season_home_away_goal_averages t WHERE (t.league_id, t.league_name, t.season) IN (SELECT league_id, league_name, season FROM league_season_home_away_goal_averages GROUP BY league_id, league_name, season HAVING COUNT(*)>1)

tests.purpose: avg_home_goals matches AVG(home_team_goal) computed from Match for that league-season.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM league_season_home_away_goal_averages v LEFT JOIN (SELECT league_id, season, AVG(home_team_goal) AS exp_avg_home FROM "Match" GROUP BY league_id, season) m ON v.league_id = m.league_id AND v.season = m.season WHERE (m.exp_avg_home IS NULL AND v.avg_home_goals IS NOT NULL) OR (m.exp_avg_home IS NOT NULL AND ABS(v.avg_home_goals - m.exp_avg_home) > 1e-6)

tests.purpose: avg_away_goals matches AVG(away_team_goal) computed from Match for that league-season.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM league_season_home_away_goal_averages v LEFT JOIN (SELECT league_id, season, AVG(away_team_goal) AS exp_avg_away FROM "Match" GROUP BY league_id, season) m ON v.league_id = m.league_id AND v.season = m.season WHERE (m.exp_avg_away IS NULL AND v.avg_away_goals IS NOT NULL) OR (m.exp_avg_away IS NOT NULL AND ABS(v.avg_away_goals - m.exp_avg_away) > 1e-6)

views.name: team_chance_creation_passing_class
views.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT t.team_api_id, t.team_short_name, ta.chanceCreationPassingClass
FROM Team t
JOIN Team_Attributes ta
  ON t.team_api_id = ta.team_api_id
views.description: Mapping of teams to their chance creation passing classification from team attributes, usable to filter teams by their chanceCreationPassingClass
validated_on: What are the short name of team who played safe while creating chance of passing?

provenance.question: List the football teams that has a chance creation passing class of Risky. Inidcate its short name only.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Return the short names of all football teams whose chance creation passing class is Risky.
Required outputs: team_short_name (short name of the team)
Filters: chanceCreationPassingClass = 'Risky'

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (team_api_id, team_short_name, chanceCreationPassingClass).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT team_api_id, team_short_name, chanceCreationPassingClass, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM team_chance_creation_passing_class GROUP BY team_api_id, team_short_name, chanceCreationPassingClass HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Every row in the view matches a join pair that actually exists in the base tables (no phantom rows).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM team_chance_creation_passing_class v LEFT JOIN Team t ON v.team_api_id = t.team_api_id LEFT JOIN Team_Attributes ta ON v.team_api_id = ta.team_api_id AND v.chanceCreationPassingClass = ta.chanceCreationPassingClass WHERE t.team_api_id IS NULL OR ta.team_api_id IS NULL

tests.purpose: Keys from Team (team_api_id, team_short_name) are not NULL in the view.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM team_chance_creation_passing_class WHERE team_api_id IS NULL OR team_short_name IS NULL

positive_subgoals:
Task: Select the team short names for teams whose chanceCreationPassingClass is 'Safe'.
Required outputs: team_short_name
Filters: chanceCreationPassingClass = 'Safe'

views.name: league_by_country
views.body_sql:
SELECT League.id AS league_id, League.name AS league_name, League.country_id AS country_id, Country.name AS country_name
FROM League
JOIN Country ON League.country_id = Country.id
views.description: All leagues with their associated country ids and country names to support queries that need leagues filtered or joined by country.
counter_examples: Which country is the league Italy Serie A from?

provenance.question: What is the name of the football league in the country of Netherlands?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the name of the football league (League.name) that is located in the country with the name 'Netherlands'.
Required outputs: League.name
Filters: Country.name = 'Netherlands'; League.country_id matches Country.id

tests.purpose: No duplicate league_id in the view (ensures grain keyed by league_id)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT league_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM league_by_country GROUP BY league_id HAVING cnt <> 1)

tests.purpose: Every view row's country_id matches an existing Country and the country_name matches that Country (checks join correctness)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM league_by_country v LEFT JOIN Country c ON v.country_id = c.id WHERE c.id IS NULL OR (v.country_name IS NOT NULL AND v.country_name <> c.name) OR (v.country_name IS NULL AND c.name IS NOT NULL)

tests.purpose: No NULL league_id or NULL country_id in the view (keys and required foreign key must be present)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM league_by_country WHERE league_id IS NULL OR country_id IS NULL

negative_subgoals:
Task: Find the country associated with the league whose name is 'Italy Serie A'.
Required outputs: country (the country that the league 'Italy Serie A' is from)
Filters: League.name = 'Italy Serie A'

views.name: player_min_height
views.body_sql: SELECT player_api_id, player_name, height FROM Player WHERE height IS NOT NULL AND height = (SELECT MIN(height) FROM Player WHERE height IS NOT NULL)
views.description: Per-dataset relation listing player identifiers with the minimum non-null height value in the Player table (shortest players).

provenance.question: Which football player has the shortest height?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the football player record(s) whose height is the minimum height value (i.e., the shortest height) in the dataset.
Required outputs: player identifier (e.g., player name or id) as present in the schema; height
Filters: height IS NOT NULL; height = MIN(height) over the entire table (i.e., equal to the smallest numeric height value present)

tests.purpose: No NULL keys: player_api_id must not be NULL in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_min_height WHERE player_api_id IS NULL

tests.purpose: All rows correspond to players whose height equals the global non-NULL minimum height in Player
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_min_height pmh WHERE pmh.height IS NULL OR pmh.height <> (SELECT MIN(height) FROM Player WHERE height IS NOT NULL)

tests.purpose: View rows are a subset of Player rows with matching player_api_id and player_name and height (no spurious rows or mismatched attributes)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_min_height pmh LEFT JOIN Player p ON p.player_api_id = pmh.player_api_id AND (p.height = pmh.height AND p.player_name = pmh.player_name) WHERE p.player_api_id IS NULL

views.name: team_home_goal_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT t.team_api_id, t.team_short_name, m.match_api_id, m.home_team_api_id, m.home_team_goal
FROM Team t
JOIN "Match" m ON m.home_team_api_id = t.team_api_id
views.description: Join of teams to matches giving each team's short name with the corresponding match's home team goal and ids to allow filtering by goal or joining to match details

provenance.question: List all the short name of the football team that had a home team goal of 10?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Select the team_short_name values for all football teams whose home_team_goal equals 10.
Required outputs: team_short_name
Filters: home_team_goal = 10

tests.purpose: View rows must be keyed by match_api_id (no duplicate match_api_id in the view)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT match_api_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM team_home_goal_join GROUP BY match_api_id HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Every view row's home_team_api_id and home_team_goal must match the Match table for the same match_api_id (measure reconciliation)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM team_home_goal_join v LEFT JOIN "Match" m ON v.match_api_id = m.match_api_id WHERE NOT (m.home_team_api_id IS v.home_team_api_id OR (m.home_team_api_id IS NULL AND v.home_team_api_id IS NULL)) OR NOT (m.home_team_goal IS v.home_team_goal OR (m.home_team_goal IS NULL AND v.home_team_goal IS NULL))

tests.purpose: Join should not produce rows with NULL match_api_id (key not NULL)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM team_home_goal_join WHERE match_api_id IS NULL

views.name: matches_per_league_season
views.body_sql: SELECT league_id, season, COUNT(*) AS match_count FROM "Match" GROUP BY league_id, season
views.description: Count of matches per league for each season (one row per league-season with match count), usable to compare or rank leagues by match totals in a season.

provenance.question: Which league had the most matches in the 2008/2009 season?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find which league had the largest number of matches in the 2008/2009 season by returning the league identifier(s) with the maximum match count for that season.
Required outputs: league_id (the identifier of the league); match_count (the number of matches in that league during the 2008/2009 season)
Filters: season = '2008/2009'; consider only matches that are counted toward a league's match total (no additional match-type filtering specified)
Sort/limit: order by match_count DESC limit 1 (return the league(s) with the maximum match_count for the specified season)

tests.purpose: View has one row per league_id+season (no duplicate league-season keys)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT league_id, season, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM matches_per_league_season GROUP BY league_id, season HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: match_count equals the number of Match rows for that league_id and season (measure reconciliation)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM matches_per_league_season v LEFT JOIN (SELECT league_id, season, COUNT(*) AS expected_count FROM "Match" GROUP BY league_id, season) b ON v.league_id = b.league_id AND v.season = b.season WHERE b.expected_count IS NULL OR v.match_count != b.expected_count

tests.purpose: Keys league_id and season are NOT NULL in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM matches_per_league_season WHERE league_id IS NULL OR season IS NULL

views.name: player_average_overall_rating
views.body_sql:
SELECT p.player_api_id, p.player_name, AVG(pa.overall_rating) AS average_overall_rating
FROM Player_Attributes pa
JOIN Player p ON pa.player_api_id = p.player_api_id
GROUP BY p.player_api_id, p.player_name
views.description: Per-player average of overall_rating from Player_Attributes joined to Player, useful for questions asking about a player's mean overall rating across records.

provenance.question: Calculate the average overall rating of Pietro Marino.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Compute the average overall rating for the player named 'Pietro Marino'.
Required outputs: average_overall_rating: a single numeric value equal to AVG(T1.overall_rating) for rows matching the filters
Filters: player_name = 'Pietro Marino'

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (player_api_id, player_name)
